You are researching Minecraft server software for a hosting company building one-click "game mode presets" on top of the itzg/docker-minecraft-server Docker image (env vars: TYPE=PAPER, SPIGET_RESOURCES=<comma-separated SpigotMC resource IDs>, MODRINTH_PROJECTS=<comma-separated modrinth slugs>, DATAPACKS=<url>).

Today is August 2026. Research these 4 genres: **SkyWars, BedWars, Survival Games / Hunger Games, and "MiniGames hub" (multiple minigames in one server)**.

For EACH genre report:
1. One-sentence definition.
2. THE single most popular / stable / actively-maintained implementation, with EXACT SpigotMC numeric resource ID and/or Modrinth project slug. List required companion plugins.
3. Server platform: Paper/Spigot vs Vanilla vs Fabric/Forge.
4. Real gotchas — these arena minigames almost always need PRE-BUILT ARENA MAPS and manual arena setup, which is a huge deal for a "one-click preset" (a fresh server with the plugin installed is NOT playable). Be explicit about which ones ship with maps / have auto-download map systems vs which require the admin to build/import maps by hand. Also flag world-management dependencies (Multiverse-Core, SlimeWorldManager), and premium/paid-only plugins.
5. Confidence it is real & actively maintained TODAY, with evidence (last update date, downloads).

CRITICAL VERIFICATION — do not guess IDs:
- Verify every SpigotMC resource ID via `https://api.spiget.org/v2/resources/<ID>` (public JSON: name, tag, downloads, updateDate unix epoch, premium flag, external download flag). Confirm name matches; convert updateDate to a human date. If `premium: true` or external download, SAY SO — SPIGET_RESOURCES cannot fetch premium/external resources.
- Verify every Modrinth slug via `https://api.modrinth.com/v2/project/<slug>` (title, downloads, updated, game_versions, loaders).
- Also WebSearch for reputation/current-status context (SpigotMC, Modrinth, r/admincraft, Apex/Shockbyte/BisectHosting one-click docs).

Candidates to verify (don't assume; look for better options too):
- SkyWars: "Advanced SkyWars" / SkyWarsReloaded (likely abandoned) / "SkyWars" by Yannicklamprecht / VoidSpawn. Find what is actually maintained in 2026.
- BedWars: BedWars1058, BedWarsRel (old), BedWars2023/BedWarsProxy, "MBedwars" (premium). Check maintenance + whether free versions exist and whether they auto-generate arenas.
- Survival Games: SurvivalGames plugins on Spigot, "Hunger Games" plugins. Most are dead — verify honestly.
- MiniGames hub: "Minigames" plugin by AddstarMC (Spigot), NexusMinigames, "MCore"/"Arcade". Also consider that real hosts implement hubs with a proxy (Velocity/BungeeCord) + separate servers, which is a big architectural gotcha for a single-container preset — call that out.

Be honest and skeptical: if a genre has NO good free actively-maintained one-click option, say so plainly and recommend the least-bad path (or recommend not shipping a preset). Flag anything last updated before ~2024.

Return a compact structured report with exact IDs, dates, and source URLs. No files — text output only.

content.text:
I have all four genres verified first-hand via the Spiget, Modrinth, Hangar and GitHub APIs. Here is the report.

## Verification method
Every ID/slug below was pulled live from `api.spiget.org/v2/resources/<id>`, `api.modrinth.com/v2/project/<slug>`, `hangar.papermc.io/api/v1/projects` and `api.github.com` on 2026-08-24. Dates are converted from the APIs' own fields, not recalled.

**Note on MC versioning:** Minecraft is now on calendar versions (26.1, 26.2). This is the single sharpest filter — several "maintained" plugins top out at 1.21.x and will not run on a current Paper server.

---

## 1. BedWars — the ONLY genre I'd ship a preset for

**Definition:** Teams defend a bed that makes them respawnable; break the enemy bed to make their deaths permanent, last team alive wins.

**Winner: Screaming BedWars (ScreamingSandals)**
- SpigotMC **63714** — name "Screaming BedWars [1.8.8 - 26.2]", 503,460 downloads, updated **2026-06-19**, `premium: false`, **`external: false`** → `SPIGET_RESOURCES=63714` works.
- Modrinth slug **`screamingbedwars`** — 17,906 dl, updated 2026-06-19, latest `0.2.44`, game_versions through **26.2**, loaders bukkit/paper/purpur/spigot.
- Also on Hangar: `ScreamingSandals/ScreamingBedWars`.
- GitHub `ScreamingSandals/BedWars`: 330 stars, **pushed 2026-08-04**, not archived.

**Platform:** Paper (Spigot/Purpur/Bukkit also fine). Standalone single container — no proxy required.

**Companions:** Multiverse-Core (to load arena worlds) — use Modrinth **`multiverse-core`** (755,795 dl, updated **2026-08-24**, supports 26.2). Do **not** use SpigotMC 390 for Multiverse: it is `external: true` and SPIGET cannot fetch it. Optional: PlaceholderAPI (Spigot **6245**, 2,147,472 dl, updated 2026-07-11, non-external, tested on 26.2), Vault (Spigot **34315**, non-external but itself last updated 2020-07-17), Citizens for NPC shop entities.

**Gotchas:**
- **Ships zero maps.** Docs are explicit that arena tutorials "presume you already have a world with your desired BedWars map." A fresh install is unplayable.
- Setup is a manual command wizard: `/bw admin <arena> add` → `pos1`/`pos2` → `team add` (≥2) → team spawns/beds → `spawner add` → `store add` → lobby/spectator → save. Realistically 20–45 min per arena for someone who knows what they're doing.
- Good news: it **rebuilds arenas internally** ("Arena rebuilding (incredibly quick)"). Multiverse/SlimeWorldManager is only needed to *load* the map world, not to restore it. Advanced SlimeWorldManager (Spigot 87209) is `external: true` anyway → not SPIGET-installable.

**Runner-up: BedWars1058** — Spigot **97320** (264,057 dl, updated **2025-02-09**, non-external), Modrinth **`bedwars1058`** (38,796 dl, updated 2025-05-25, **game_versions stop at 1.21.4**). GitHub pushed 2026-06-22, latest release 25.9 (2025-09-13). Supports SHARED/MULTIARENA modes so it runs standalone without a proxy — but it is behind on 26.x, which disqualifies it for a current-version preset.

**MBedwars is premium** — €20 via BuiltByBit / mbedwars.com. Cannot be auto-installed by SPIGET_RESOURCES or MODRINTH_PROJECTS. It surfaced on a nulled-plugin forum in search results; shipping cracked jars to customers is a legal and malware liability, so treat that as off-limits.

**BedWarsRel (Spigot 6799) is dead** — last updated 2017-07-04 and `external: true`.

---

## 2. Survival Games / Hunger Games — one genuinely viable option

**Definition:** Battle-royale — players spawn on pedestals around a loot-filled map, race for chests, and fight until one survivor remains as the border/deathmatch closes in.

**Winner: HungerGames (ShaneBeeStudios)**
- Modrinth slug **`hungergames-sb`** — 1,395 dl, updated **2026-07-28**, latest `5.1.1`, **game_versions 1.21.4 → 26.2**, loader **paper only**. Direct CDN jar confirmed.
- GitHub `ShaneBeeStudios/HungerGames`: 38 stars, pushed **2026-07-28**, releases 5.1.1 (2026-07-28), 5.1.0 (2026-07-25), 5.0.0 (2026-05-05) — genuinely active cadence.
- **Use MODRINTH_PROJECTS, not SPIGET.** The SpigotMC page in this lineage (**65942**, JT122406 fork, 87,134 dl) last updated **2023-07-23** and is stale.

**Platform:** Paper only (`loaders: ["paper"]`).

**Companions:** None required — no WorldEdit/Multiverse/Vault hard deps. This is the lightest-dependency plugin in the whole report.

**Gotchas:**
- **No maps ship.** Setup = build the arena yourself, place normal and bonus chests, then `/hg create <name> <min> <max> <time> [cost]`, select corners with a stick, and **right-click every single spawn point individually**. For a 24-player map that's 24 manual clicks.
- Supports multiple arenas, kits and teams in one server; no proxy needed.

**Everything else in this genre is dead** — Survival Games Reloaded (Spigot 17740, updated 2020-01-19, `external: true`), BukkitGames (Spigot 279, updated 2018-01-20), Lib's Hungergames (Spigot 55, updated 2014). The Ayman-Isam "Hunger Games" (Modrinth `hungergames`, 9,393 dl — the highest download count in the genre) is updated 2026-01-06 but **tops out at 1.21.11 with no 26.x support**, and its Spigot listing 111936 is `external: true`.

---

## 4. MiniGames hub — architecturally wrong for a single container. Don't ship it.

**Definition:** One server/network offering many different minigames (spleef, TNT run, parkour, quake…) selectable from a central lobby hub.

**There is no maintained free single-container implementation.**
- **Minigames by AddstarMC** — Spigot **19687**, 73,973 dl, SpigotMC page last updated **2018-01-13**. GitHub pushed 2024-12-20 but **last GitHub release was 2018** (`1.12.2-SNAPSHOT`). Effectively abandoned for modern MC.
- **MinigamesLib** — Spigot 23844, 457,854 dl, updated 2017-06-12. Dead.
- **Party Games X** (Spigot 83240) and **Arcade Minigames** (Spigot 49093) are both `premium: true` → not fetchable by SPIGET.
- **BattleArena** — Modrinth `battlearena`, 12,574 dl, updated 2026-08-05, supports 26.2, GitHub pushed 2026-08-05. But it only publishes **SNAPSHOT builds** (`4.0.5-SNAPSHOT-106`), its modes are all PvP variants (Arena, Skirmish, Colosseum, FFA, Deathmatch, Tournament) rather than a Hypixel-style hub, and it still needs arenas defined manually. Its Spigot listing (2164) is `external: true`.
- Hangar has nothing viable — the top "minigame" hit is `Kr0tex_/MinigamesHub` with **4 downloads**.

**The architectural gotcha:** real minigame networks run a **Velocity/BungeeCord proxy plus N separate backend Paper servers**, one per game type, with players transferred between them. Both BedWars plugins expose this directly (BedWars1058 has BUNGEE/BUNGEE-LEGACY modes; Screaming BedWars advertises BungeeCord/Velocity support). A single `itzg/docker-minecraft-server` container is one JVM running one Paper server — it structurally cannot be a hub. Selling a "MiniGames hub" preset as one container would misrepresent the product.

## The bigger finding: how competitors actually do "one-click"

Apex Hosting's BedWars and SkyWars gametypes ship **"all of the required worlds, files, and plugins preconfigured"** — a pre-made lobby and ready-built arenas. They are not installing a plugin jar; they are deploying a **whole server pack**. Plugin-ID env vars alone can never match that, because the maps are the product.

`itzg` already supports this and it's the right mechanism for you:
- **`GENERIC_PACK`/`GENERIC_PACKS`** — URL(s) to a zip overlaid onto the server directory (can carry plugins, configs *and* a completed `arenas/` config). Multiple entries applied in order; supports OCI, URL and local-path entries.
- **`WORLD`** — URL of a zip/tar world archive; it locates `level.dat` and moves that directory into `$LEVEL`.

So the real work for a BedWars preset is: build (or license) 2–3 arena maps once, complete the `/bw admin` setup once, then tarball the world + `plugins/BedWars/arenas/` config and serve it via `GENERIC_PACK`. That is a content/build task, not a plugin-selection task.

Also confirmed from the itzg docs: SPIGET can't fetch everything — it explicitly warns "Some plugins, such as EssentialsX (resource ID 9089), do not permit automated downloads via Spiget," and recommends mounting `/plugins` for those.
